metadata.title: Weighted Minkowski's Existence Theorem and Projection Bodies

nodes.name: Convex body and support function
nodes.statement: A convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a convex, compact set with nonempty interior; for $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$, its support function is $h_K(x)=\sup_{y\in K}\langle x,y\rangle$.

nodes.name: Star body, radial function, Minkowski functional
nodes.statement: A star body $L$ has continuous radial function $\rho_L(y)=\sup\{\lambda:\lambda y\in L\}$; for $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ the Minkowski functional is $\|y\|_K=\rho_K^{-1}(y)$.

nodes.name: Surface area measure $S_K$
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ and Borel $A\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$: $S_K(A)=\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(n_K^{-1}(A))$, where $n_K:\partial K\to\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is the Gauss map.

nodes.name: Curvature function $f_K$
nodes.statement: For $K$ of class $C^2_+$, $dS_K(\theta)=f_K(\theta)d\theta$, where $f_K=\det(D^2 h_K + h_K I)$ is the reciprocal of the Gauss curvature as a function of the outer unit normal.

nodes.name: Wulff shape
nodes.statement: For positive $f\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$, the Wulff shape is $[f]=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle x,u\rangle\le f(u)\;\forall u\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\}$.

nodes.name: Mixed volume $V(K,L)$
nodes.statement: $V(K,L)=\frac{1}{n}\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}\frac{\mathrm{Vol}_n(K+\epsilon L)-\mathrm{Vol}_n(K)}{\epsilon}=\frac{1}{n}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}h_L(u)dS_K(u)$.

nodes.name: Projection body $\Pi K$
nodes.statement: $\Pi K$ is the symmetric convex body with support function $h_{\Pi K}(\theta)=\mathrm{Vol}_{n-1}(P_{\theta^\perp}K)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}|\langle\theta,u\rangle|dS_K(u)$.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-homogeneous measure
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\alpha>0$, if $\mu(tK)=t^\alpha\mu(K)$ for all Borel $K$ in supp$(\mu)$ and $t>0$; its density $\phi$ is then $(\alpha-n)$-homogeneous.

nodes.name: $s$-concave measure
nodes.statement: $\mu$ is $s$-concave on $\mathcal{C}$ if $\mu(tA+(1-t)B)\geq(t\mu(A)^s+(1-t)\mu(B)^s)^{1/s}$ for $A,B\in\mathcal{C}$, $t\in[0,1]$, with limiting cases log-concave ($s=0$) and $\min$-concave ($s=-\infty$).

nodes.name: Weighted surface area measure $S^\mu_K$
nodes.statement: For Borel $E\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$: $S^\mu_K(E)=\int_{n_K^{-1}(E)}\phi(y)dy$; if $K\in C^2_+$ then $dS^\mu_K(u)=\phi(n_K^{-1}(u))f_K(u)du$.

nodes.name: The class $\Lambda^n$
nodes.statement: $\Lambda^n=\{\mu \text{ Borel with continuous density}:\exists\beta>0,\;\lim_{r\to\infty}\mu(rB_2^n)^{\beta/n}/r=0,\;\lim_{r\to 0}\mu(rB_2^n)^{\beta/n}/r=\infty\}$.

nodes.name: Weighted projection body $\Pi_\mu K$
nodes.statement: $\Pi_\mu K$ is the convex body with support function $h_{\Pi_\mu K}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\partial K}|\langle\theta,n_K(y)\rangle|\phi(y)dy=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}|\langle\theta,u\rangle|dS^\mu_K(u)$.

nodes.name: $F$-concave measure
nodes.statement: $\mu$ is $F$-concave on a class $\mathcal{C}$, with $F$ invertible and monotone, if $\mu((1-\lambda)K+\lambda L)\geq F^{-1}((1-\lambda)F(\mu(K))+\lambda F(\mu(L)))$ for $K,L\in\mathcal{C}$, $\lambda\in(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Mixed measure $\mu(K,L)$
nodes.statement: For $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ and Borel $\mu$ with density: $\mu(K,L)=\liminf_{\epsilon\to 0}(\mu(K+\epsilon L)-\mu(K))/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Cosine transform
nodes.statement:
For $f\in L^1(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$: $\mathcal{C}(f)(	heta)=\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}|\langle	heta,uangle|f(u)du$; for a signed Borel measure $
u$: $\mathcal{C}(d
u)(	heta)=\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}|\langle	heta,uangle|d
u$.

nodes.name: Weighted projective class $\mathcal{P}_\mu K$
nodes.statement: For Borel $\mu$ with continuous density, $\mathcal{P}_\mu K=\{L\in\mathcal{K}^n:\Pi_\mu L=\Pi_\mu K\}$.

nodes.name: $\mu$-Blaschke body $\nabla_\mu K$
nodes.statement: $\nabla_\mu K$ is the convex body whose $\mu$-surface area measure equals $\frac{1}{2}(dS^\mu_K(u)+dS^\mu_K(-u))$.

nodes.name: $\beta$-$\mu$-Blaschke body $\nabla_{\mu,\beta}K$
nodes.statement: For $\mu\in\Lambda^n$ with $\beta>0$: the symmetric convex body satisfying $\mu(\nabla_{\mu,\beta}K)^{\beta/n-1}dS^\mu_{\nabla_{\mu,\beta}K}(u)=\frac{\mu(K)^{\beta/n-1}}{2}(dS^\mu_K(u)+dS^\mu_K(-u))$.

nodes.name: Banach-Mazur distance and $d_\Pi(L)$
nodes.statement: $d_{BM}(L,M)=\inf\{d>0:\exists T\in GL_n,L\subset TM\subset dL\}$ and $d_\Pi(L)=\inf\{d_{BM}(L,M):M \text{ a projection body}\}$; satisfies $1\le d_\Pi(L)\le\sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Harmonic function and mean value property
nodes.statement: $u\in C^2(\overline{\Omega})$ is harmonic if $\triangle u=0$ on $\Omega$; equivalently, $u(x)=\frac{1}{r^n\kappa_n}\int_{B(x,r)}u(y)dy$ for every ball $B(x,r)\subset\Omega$.

nodes.name: $p$-capacity
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Cap}_p(\Omega)=\inf\{\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla v|^p dx:v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n),v\geq 1\text{ on }\Omega\}$; $\mathrm{Cap}_2$ is the Newton capacity.

nodes.name: $p$-capacitary measure
nodes.statement: For Borel $E\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$: $\mu_p(\Omega,E)=(p-1)\int_{n_\Omega^{-1}(E)}|\nabla u(y)|^p dy$, where $u$ is the $p$-capacitary function.

nodes.name: Mixed $p$-capacity
nodes.statement: For bounded convex domains $\Omega_0,\Omega_1$: $C_p(\Omega_0,\Omega_1)=\frac{1}{n-p}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}h_{\Omega_1}(\xi)d\mu_p(\Omega_0,\xi)$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Minkowski addition (Firey)
nodes.statement: For $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, $q\geq 1$: $\alpha\cdot K+_q\beta\cdot L$ has support function $h^q_{\alpha\cdot K+_q\beta\cdot L}(x)=\alpha h_K^q(x)+\beta h_L^q(x)$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ surface area measure
nodes.statement: $dS_{K,q}(u)=h_K^{1-q}(u)dS_K(u)$, satisfying $\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}(\mathrm{Vol}_n(K+_q\epsilon\cdot B_2^n)-\mathrm{Vol}_n(K))/\epsilon=\frac{1}{q}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}dS_{K,q}(u)$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ weighted surface area measure $S^\mu_{K,q}$
nodes.statement: For Borel $E\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$: $S^\mu_{K,q}(E)=\int_{n_K^{-1}(E)\cap\partial' K}\phi(x)h_K^{1-q}(n_K(y))dy$.

nodes.name: $L^q$-mixed measure $\mu_q(K,L)$
nodes.statement: $\mu_q(K,L):=\liminf_{\epsilon\to 0}(\mu(K+_q\epsilon\cdot L)-\mu(K))/\epsilon=\frac{1}{q}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}h_L(u)^q dS^\mu_{K,q}(u)$.

nodes.name: Weighted Minkowski Existence Question
nodes.statement: Given Borel $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with locally integrable density and finite, even Borel $\nu$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ not concentrated on any great hemisphere, does there exist symmetric $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and constant $c_{\mu,K}$ with $d\nu(u)=c_{\mu,K}dS^\mu_K(u)$?

nodes.statement:
For Borel $\mu,
u$ with continuous densities and symmetric $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $h_{\Pi_\mu K}(	heta)\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}(	heta)$ for all $	heta\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, does $\mathcal{A}>0$ exist with $\mu(K)\leq\mathcal{A}
u(L)$?

nodes.name: Capacity Shephard Question
nodes.statement:
For $p,q\in(1,n)$, symmetric $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ and the measures with densities $|
abla u|^p,|
abla v|^q$ generated by $p$- and $q$-capacitary functions of $K,L$: if $h_{\Pi_\mu K}(	heta)\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}(	heta)$, does $\mathcal{M}>0$ exist with $C_p(\mathrm{int}(K))\leq\mathcal{M}C_p(\mathrm{int}(L))$?

nodes.name: Minkowski's Existence Theorem (classical)
nodes.statement: If a finite Borel $\mu$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is not concentrated on any great hemisphere and is centered ($\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}\xi d\mu(\xi)=0$), then there exists a unique (up to translation) convex body $K$ with $dS_K=d\mu$.

nodes.name: Borell's classification of $s$-concave measures
nodes.statement: A Radon $s$-concave measure $\mu$ on Borel subsets of an open convex $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has density $f$ with $d\mu=f dx_\Omega$, and $f$ obeys the case-table relations between $s$ and the convexity/concavity of $f^{s/(1-sd)}$.
conclusions: case relations: $s<0\Leftrightarrow f^{s/(1-sd)}$ convex; $s=0\Leftrightarrow\log f$ concave; $0<s<1/d\Leftrightarrow f^{s/(1-sd)}$ concave; $s=1/d\Leftrightarrow f$ constant; $s>1/d\Leftrightarrow f=0$ a.e.

nodes.name: Livshyts' weighted Minkowski existence
nodes.statement: For $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\alpha>n$, Borel $\mu$ with density $\phi$ that is $p$-concave ($p\geq 0$) on a half-space, and even $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ with $\mathrm{supp}(\varphi)\subset\mathrm{int}(\mathrm{supp}(\phi))\cap\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, there exists a unique (up to $\mu$-zero) $K$ with $dS^\mu_K(u)=d\varphi(u)$.

nodes.name: Minkowski's Inequality (classical)
nodes.statement: For $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$: $V(K,L)^n\geq\mathrm{Vol}_n(K)^{n-1}\mathrm{Vol}_n(L)$.

nodes.name: Ehrhard's Inequality
nodes.statement: For $0<t<1$ and closed convex $K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$: $\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n((1-t)K+tL))\geq(1-t)\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n(K))+t\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n(L))$, where $\Phi(x)=\gamma_1((-\infty,x))$.

nodes.name: Single-point equality propagates in $F$-concavity
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $F$-concave with $F$ monotone on $\mathcal{C}$ and equality holds in the $F$-concavity inequality for some $\lambda\in(0,1)$, then equality holds for all $\lambda\in[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Milman-Rotem equality conditions for $s$-concavity
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $s$-concave on Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($s\in[-\infty,1/n]$) and equality holds at some $t\in(0,1)$ for Borel $A,B$ with $\mu(A)\mu(B)>0$, then $A=\alpha B+\beta$ and $\varphi(\alpha x+\beta)=c\varphi(x)$ a.e. on $B$.

nodes.name: Polar-cone identity (HLYZ Lemma 2.9)
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ and $f:\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}^+$: $\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}f(u)\rho_K^n(u)du=\int_{\partial' K}\langle x,n_K(x)\rangle f(x/|x|)dx$.

nodes.name: Jacobian of $r_K$
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$, the Jacobian of $r_K:\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\to\partial K$ is $\rho_K^n(u)/h_K(n_K(r_K(u)))$ a.e.

nodes.name: First Variation of Radial Functions of Wulff Shapes
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ and $f\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ there is $\delta,M>0$ so that $h_t=h_K+tf>0$ and $|\rho_{[h_t]}(u)-\rho_K(u)|<M|t|$ for $|t|<\delta$, with $\partial_t\rho_{[h_t]}|_{t=0}=f(n_K(r_K(u)))\rho_K(u)/h_K(n_K(r_K(u)))$ a.e.

nodes.name: Aleksandrov's Variational Formula for Arbitrary Measures
nodes.statement: For Borel $\mu$ with locally integrable density $\phi$, $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $\partial K$ in the Lebesgue set of $\phi$, and $f\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$: $\lim_{t\to 0}(\mu([h_K+tf])-\mu(K))/t=\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}f(u)dS^\mu_K(u)$.
assumptions: $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $\partial K$ in Lebesgue set of $\phi$

nodes.name: Representation of Mixed Measures
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$, compact convex $L$, and $\mu$ with density $\phi$ such that $K\subset\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ and $\partial K$ is in the Lebesgue set of $\phi$: $\mu(K,L)=\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}h_L(u)dS^\mu_K(u)$, equal to $\int h_L\phi(n_K^{-1})f_K du$ when $K\in C^2_+$.
assumptions: $\mu$ has density $\phi$, $K\subset\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$, $\partial K$ in Lebesgue set of $\phi$

nodes.name: Minkowski's Inequality for $F$-Concave Measures
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $F$-concave with $F$ differentiable on $\mathcal{C}$, then for $K,L\in\mathcal{C}$: $\mu(K,L)\geq\mu(K,K)+(F(\mu(L))-F(\mu(K)))/F'(\mu(K))$.

nodes.name: Minkowski's Inequality - Concavity link
nodes.statement: For $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ and $\mu$ $F$-concave with $F$ differentiable: equality in Minkowski's inequality (Theorem 2.5) holds iff equality holds in the defining $F$-concavity inequality.
conclusions: equality in Minkowski's inequality $\Leftrightarrow$ equality in $F$-concavity

nodes.name: Uniqueness inequality from $F$-concavity
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $F$-concave with $F$ differentiable and $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ satisfy $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then $(F(\mu(L))-F(\mu(K)))/F'(\mu(K))\leq(F(\mu(L))-F(\mu(K)))/F'(\mu(L))$.

nodes.name: Equality in Minkowski under equal mass
nodes.statement: If $\mu(K)=\mu(L)$ and $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then equality holds in Minkowski's inequality and consequently in the $F$-concavity inequality.

nodes.name: Uniqueness from monotone-derivative $F$
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $F$-concave with $F$ differentiable, $(F(b)-F(c))(F'(b)-F'(c))\geq 0$, $F'(b)F'(c)>0$, $F'(b)\neq F'(c)$ for $b,c\in[a,\mu(\mathbb{R}^n))$, and $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ with $\mu(K),\mu(L)\geq a$ satisfy $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then $\mu(K)=\mu(L)$ and equality in $F$-concavity.

nodes.name: Functional families satisfying Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: $F$ increasing strictly convex on $[a,\mu(\mathbb{R}^n))$, or $F$ decreasing strictly concave on $[a,\mu(\mathbb{R}^n))$, satisfy the hypotheses of the uniqueness lemma.

nodes.name: Gaussian uniqueness on $\{\gamma_n\geq 1/2\}$
nodes.statement: If $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ with $\gamma_n(K),\gamma_n(L)\geq 1/2$ and $dS^{\gamma_n}_K=dS^{\gamma_n}_L$, then $K=L$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness inequality for $\alpha$-homogeneous, $p$-concave
nodes.statement: If a Radon $\mu$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\alpha>0$, and $p$-concave, and $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ satisfy $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then $\mu(K)-\mu(L)\geq(\mu^p(K)-\mu^p(L))/(\alpha p\mu^{p-1}(L))$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness when $p\alpha=1$
nodes.statement: If a Radon $\mu$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\alpha>0$, and $1/\alpha$-concave, and $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ satisfy $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then $\mu(K)=\mu(L)$ and $K=aL+b$ $\mu$-a.e. for some $a\in\mathbb{R}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Centred bodies coincide
nodes.statement: Under Lemma 2.11 with $K,L$ centred ($\int_K x dx=0$, etc.), we get $b=0$, $a=1$, hence $K=L$.

nodes.name: Concavity-promotion (Livshyts A.2)
nodes.statement: If $g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^+$ is $s$-concave and $r$-homogeneous with $s,r>0$, then $g$ is also $1/r$-concave.

nodes.name: Uniqueness for $\alpha$-homogeneous, $p$-concave measures
nodes.statement: Let Radon $\mu$ be $\alpha$-homogeneous and $p$-concave with either $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p=1/\alpha$. If centred $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ satisfy $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$, then $K=L$.

nodes.name: Weighted Minkowski Existence Theorem ($\Lambda^n$)
nodes.statement: For Borel $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with even continuous density and $\mu\in\Lambda^n$ for some $\beta>0$, and finite even $\nu$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ not concentrated on any hemisphere: there exists symmetric $K$ with $d\nu(u)=c_{\mu,K}dS^\mu_K(u)$, $c_{\mu,K}=\mu(K)^{\beta/n-1}$.
assumptions: $\mu$ Borel with even continuous density, $\mu\in\Lambda^n$ for some $\beta>0$
$\nu$ finite even on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, not concentrated on any hemisphere

nodes.name: Proof of Weighted Minkowski Existence
nodes.statement: Maximise the functional $\psi_{\nu,\beta}(f)=\frac{n}{\beta}\mu([f])^{\beta/n}-\int f d\nu$ over even continuous $f$; show maximisers are support functions of symmetric bodies, derive Euler-Lagrange equation via Aleksandrov's variational formula, then exhibit the maximiser via Blaschke selection in a fixed ball.

nodes.name: Define functional, show maximiser is a support function
Variational equation at the maximiser
nodes.statement: Perturb $h_t=h_{K_\beta}+tf$ and use $\partial_t\psi_{\nu,\beta}(h_t)|_{t=0}=0$ together with Lemma~LP456.2 to derive $\int f d\nu=\int f \mu(K_\beta)^{\beta/n-1}dS^\mu_{K_\beta}$ for all even $f\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$.

nodes.name: Conclude $d\nu=\mu(K_\beta)^{\beta/n-1}dS^\mu_{K_\beta}$ via Riesz
nodes.statement: Density of continuous functions in $L^1(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ and the Riesz Representation theorem upgrade the variational identity to equality of measures.

nodes.name: Bound the search domain via $q_\beta$
Maximiser exists via Blaschke selection
nodes.statement: Pick a maximising sequence $K_i$ in $\mathcal{F}=\{K=-K\subset RB_2^n\}$; Blaschke selection gives a Hausdorff limit $K_\beta\in\mathcal{F}$ with $\psi_{\nu,\beta}(h_{K_\beta})=\sup\psi_{\nu,\beta}$, and the sup-positivity ensures $K_\beta$ has nonempty interior.

nodes.name: Weak version of Theorem TP456.10
nodes.statement:
If $\lim_{r	o\infty}\mu(rB_2^n)^{ eta/n}/r<
u(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ and $\mu(rB_2^n)^{ eta/n}/r\geq
u(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ for $r\in(0,\delta)$, then symmetric $K$ exists with $d
u(u)=\mu(K)^{ eta/n-1}dS^\mu_K(u)$.

nodes.name: Constant cannot be removed for Gaussian
nodes.statement:
For $d
u(u)=t du$ with $t$ large, no $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ satisfies $d
u=dS^{\gamma_n}_K$, since $S^{\gamma_n}_K(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})\leq 4n^{1/4}$ while $
u(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ is unbounded.

nodes.name: Removal of constant for $\alpha$-homogeneous $\mu$, $\alpha\neq 1$
nodes.statement:
If even Borel $\mu$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous with $\alpha>0$, $\alpha
eq 1$, and $
u$ is finite, even, not concentrated on a hemisphere on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, then there is symmetric $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $d
u=dS^\mu_K$.
assumptions: $\nu$ finite, even, not on a hemisphere

nodes.name: $\alpha=1$ case open
nodes.statement: For $\alpha=1$, $dS^\mu_L$ is $0$-homogeneous in $L$; the dilation rescaling fails and the case remains open.

nodes.name: Existence and Uniqueness for $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous $\mu$
nodes.statement:
If a Radon $\mu$ is even, $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\alpha
eq 1$, and either $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p=1/\alpha$, and $
u$ is a finite even measure on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ not on a hemisphere, then a unique symmetric $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ satisfies $d
u=dS^\mu_K$.
assumptions: $\nu$ finite even on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$, not on hemisphere

nodes.name: Funk-Hecke uniqueness for cosine transform
nodes.statement: For bounded integrable functions or signed measures $F_1,F_2$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$: $\mathcal{C}(F_1)(\theta)=\mathcal{C}(F_2)(\theta)$ for all $\theta$ iff $F_1^+(u)=F_2^+(u)$ a.e.

nodes.name: Fourier Transform of Measures on the Sphere
nodes.statement:
For an even Borel $
u$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ with density $g$: $\widehat{
u_e}(	heta)=- rac{\pi}{2}\mathcal{C}(d
u)(	heta)$; for an even non-negative $g$: $\widehat{g}(	heta)=- rac{\pi}{2}\mathcal{C}(g)(	heta)$.

nodes.name: Spherical Parseval (KRZ)
nodes.statement: For symmetric $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ of class $C^2_+$ with $dS_K=f_K du$: $\int_{S^{n-1}}\widehat{h_L}(\theta)\widehat{f_K}(\theta)d\theta=(2\pi)^n\int_{S^{n-1}}h_L(\theta)f_K(\theta)d\theta$.

nodes.name: Classical projective class structure
nodes.statement: For $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ with projective class $\mathcal{P}K$, the Blaschke body $\nabla K$ is the unique symmetric body in $\mathcal{P}K$ and is the largest by volume.

nodes.name: Cosine-transform characterization of projection bodies
nodes.statement: $L\in\mathcal{K}^n$ is a projection body iff there is finite Borel $\nu$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ with $\int h_L(u)g(u)du=\int\mathcal{C}(g)(u)d\nu(u)$ for every even, non-negative $g\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$.

nodes.name: Existence and largeness of $\nabla_\mu K$ in $\mathcal{P}_\mu K$
nodes.statement: For Radon $\mu$ that is $p$-concave and $\alpha$-homogeneous with $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p\alpha=1$, the $\mu$-Blaschke body $\nabla_\mu K$ exists, is symmetric, unique, and $\mu$-largest in $\mathcal{P}_\mu K$, with equality iff $K$ is symmetric.

nodes.name: Shephard-type cosine bound
nodes.statement:
For Borel $\mu,
u$ with continuous densities $\phi,\psi$ and symmetric $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$: if $h_{\Pi_\mu K}(	heta)\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}(	heta)$ for all $	heta$, then $\mu(K,L)\leq d_\Pi(L)
u(L,L)$.

nodes.name: Shephard bound under $\beta$-homogeneous $\nu$
nodes.statement: If additionally $\nu$ is $\beta$-homogeneous, $\beta>0$, then $\mu(K,L)\leq\beta d_\Pi(L)\nu(L)$.

nodes.name: Shephard bound under $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous $\mu$
nodes.statement:
If $\mu$ is $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous and $
u$ is $ eta$-homogeneous, $\alpha, eta>0$, with $h_{\Pi_\mu K}\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}$, then $\mu(K)\leq[d_\Pi(L) eta p
u(L)/\mu(L)+\mu(K)(1-\alpha p)/\mu(L)]^{1/(1-p)}\mu(L)$; specially when $\alpha p=1$, $\mu(K)\leq( eta
u(L)/(\alpha\mu(L))d_\Pi(L))^{\alpha/(\alpha-1)}\mu(L)$.

nodes.name: Refined Shephard bound under volume-like $\mu$
nodes.statement:
If $\mu$ is $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous with $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p=1/\alpha$, $
u$ is $ eta$-homogeneous, $ eta>0$, and $h_{\Pi_\mu K}\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}$, then $\mu(K)\leq( eta
u(L)/(\alpha\mu(L))d_\Pi(L))^{\alpha/(\alpha-1)}\mu(L)$.

nodes.name: Isomorphic Shephard Problem for Homogeneous Measures
nodes.statement:
If $\mu,
u$ have continuous densities, $
u$ is $ eta$-homogeneous, $\mu$ is $p$-concave and $\alpha$-homogeneous with either $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p=1/\alpha$, and symmetric $K,L$ satisfy $h_{\Pi_\mu K}\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}$, then $\mu(K)\leq rac{ eta}{\alpha}\mathcal{A}d_\Pi(L)
u(L)$ with $\mathcal{A}=\min\{\mathcal{A}_K,\mathcal{A}_L\}$, $\mathcal{A}_K=(\mu(K)/\mu(L))^{1/\alpha}$, $\mathcal{A}_L=(
u(L) eta/(\mu(L)\alpha))^{1/(\alpha-1)}d_\Pi(L)^{1/(\alpha-1)}$.

nodes.name: Shephard for $\mu=\nu$
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of TP456.12 with $\mu=\nu$: $\mu(K)\leq d_\Pi(L)^{\alpha/(\alpha-1)}\mu(L)$, and $\mu(K)\leq\mu(L)$ if $L$ is a projection body.

nodes.name: Shephard bound for $F$-concave $\mu$
nodes.statement:
If Borel $\mu,
u$ with continuous densities have $\mu$ $\alpha$-homogeneous ($\alpha>1$) and $F$-concave with $1/(zF'(z))$ and $F(z)/(zF'(z))$ in $L^1_{loc}([0,\mu(\mathbb{R}^n)))$, $
u$ $ eta$-homogeneous, and symmetric $K,L$ satisfy $h_{\Pi_\mu K}\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}$, then $\mu(K)\leq\mathcal{Z}
u(L)+\mathcal{L}$ with $\mathcal{Z}= eta d_\Pi(L)/(\alpha-1)$ and $\mathcal{L}= rac{1}{\alpha}\int_0^{\mu(K)} rac{F(z)}{zF'(z)}dz- rac{F(\mu(L))}{\alpha}\int_0^{\mu(K)} rac{dz}{zF'(z)}$.

nodes.name: Shephard bound for $p$-concave $\mu$
nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of TP456.13 with $\mu$ also $p$-concave and $F(z)=z^p$: $\mu(K)\leq\mathcal{Z}
u(L)$ with $\mathcal{Z}=(
u(L)/\mu(L))^{p/(1-p)}(\alpha p eta(1-p)d_\Pi(L)/(\alpha-1)+(1-\alpha p)(1-p)\mu(K)/
u(L))^{1/(1-p)}$, simplifying to $\mathcal{Z}=(
u(L)/\mu(L))^{1/(\alpha-1)}( eta d_\Pi(L)/\alpha)^{\alpha/(\alpha-1)}$ when $\alpha p=1$.

nodes.name: John-position bounds remove $\nu/\mu$ ratios
nodes.statement:
If $L$ in John position: $
u(L)/\mu(L)\leq n^{ eta/2}
u(B_2^n)/\mu(B_2^n)$. If $K,L$ both in John position: $\mu(K)/
u(L)\leq n^{\alpha/2}\mu(B_2^n)/
u(B_2^n)$ and $\mu(K)/\mu(L)\leq n^{\alpha/2}$.

nodes.name: Stability in Isomorphic Shephard
nodes.statement:
If $
u$ is $ eta$-homogeneous, $\mu$ is $\alpha\in(0,1)\cup(1,\infty)$-homogeneous and $1/\alpha$-concave, and symmetric $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ satisfy $h_{\Pi_\mu K}\leq h_{\Pi_
u L}-\epsilon$, then $\mu(K)^{1-1/\alpha}\leq rac{ eta}{\alpha} rac{
u(L)}{\mu(L)}d_\Pi(L)\mu(L)^{1-1/\alpha}-C(\mu)\epsilon$, with $C(\mu)$ depending only on $\mu$.

nodes.name: Harmonic-density representative in $\mathcal{P}_K\mu$
nodes.statement: For symmetric $K\in C^2_+$ and even Borel $\mu$ with density continuous on $\partial K$, there is a unique even $\nu\in\mathcal{P}_K\mu$ whose density is harmonic on $\mathrm{int}(K)$.

nodes.name: Minkowski's Inequality for Capacity
nodes.statement: For $1<p<n$ and bounded convex domains $\Omega_0,\Omega_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$: $C_p(\Omega_0,\Omega_1)^{n-p}\geq C_p(\Omega_0)^{n-p-1}C_p(\Omega_1)$ with equality iff $\Omega_0,\Omega_1$ are homothetic.

nodes.name: Capacity Shephard Inequality
nodes.statement: Under Question~ProbP456.3 with $p<n-1$: $C_p(\mathrm{int}(K))\leq(\frac{p-1}{n-p}\frac{n-q}{q-1}d_\Pi(L))^{(n-p)/(n-p-1)}(C_q(\mathrm{int}(L))/C_p(\mathrm{int}(L)))^{1/(n-p-1)}C_q(\mathrm{int}(L))$; for $p\in(n-1,n)$ a symmetric inequality with $C_q(\mathrm{int}(L))$ on the left holds.
conclusions: the displayed capacity bounds; reduce to $C_p(\mathrm{int}(K))\leq C_p(\mathrm{int}(L))$ when $p=q\in(1,n-1)$ and $L$ is a projection body, and reverse when $p\in(n-1,n)$

nodes.name: Failure at $p=n-1$
nodes.statement: When $p=n-1$, Lemma~LP456.13 reduces to $C_p(\mathrm{int}(K),\mathrm{int}(L))\geq C_p(\mathrm{int}(L))$, and the schema fails.

nodes.name: $L^q$-Wulff containment
nodes.statement: For $q\geq q'\geq 1$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$: $(1-\lambda)\cdot K+_q\lambda\cdot L\supseteq(1-\lambda)\cdot K+_{q'}\lambda\cdot L\supseteq(1-\lambda)K+\lambda L$.

nodes.name: $F$-concavity transfers to $L^q$ addition
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ is $F$-concave with respect to Minkowski addition on $\mathcal{C}$, then for $q\geq 1$ and $K,L\in\mathcal{C}$, $\lambda\in[0,1]$: $\mu((1-\lambda)\cdot K+_q\lambda\cdot L)\geq F^{-1}((1-\lambda)F(\mu(K))+\lambda F(\mu(L)))$, with equality forcing equality in the original Minkowski-addition inequality.

nodes.name: $L^q$-concavities of the Gaussian measure
nodes.statement: For Borel $K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $\lambda\in(0,1)$, $q\geq 1$, $\gamma_n$ satisfies the Ehrhard inequality, log-concavity, and the Gardner-Zvavitch inequality with respect to $L^q$ addition, with the corresponding equality conditions.
nodes.origin_citation: Borell 2003; Ehrhard; Latala 1996; Borell 1975; Brascamp-Lieb 1976; Eskenazis-Moschidis 2021; Gardner-Zvavitch 2010; Kolesnikov-Livshyts 2021

nodes.name: Firey's $L^q$-Brunn-Minkowski for volume
nodes.statement: For $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$, $q>1$, $\lambda\in(0,1)$: $\mathrm{Vol}_n((1-\lambda)\cdot K+_q\lambda\cdot L)^{q/n}\geq(1-\lambda)\mathrm{Vol}_n(K)^{q/n}+\lambda\mathrm{Vol}_n(L)^{q/n}$, equality iff $K,L$ are dilates.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Weighted Minkowski Existence
nodes.statement: For $q\geq 1$, even Borel $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with continuous density and $\mu\in\Lambda^n$ for some $\beta>0$, and $\nu$ a finite, even Borel measure on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ not on a hemisphere, there is symmetric $K$ with $d\nu(u)=c_{\mu,K,q}dS^\mu_{K,q}(u)$, $c_{\mu,K,q}=\frac{1}{q}\mu(K)^{\beta/n-1}$.

nodes.name: $L^q$-First Variation of Radial Functions of Wulff Shapes
nodes.statement: Fix $q\geq 1$, $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$, $f\in C(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$. There is small $\delta>0$ so that $h_t(u)=(h_K^q(u)+tf(u))^{1/q}>0$ and $\partial_t\rho_{[h_t]}(u)|_{t=0}=\frac{1}{q}f(n_K(r_K(u)))\rho_K(u)/h_K^q(n_K(r_K(u)))$ a.e.

nodes.name: Aleksandrov's $L^q$-Variational Formula
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Lemma LP456.2 and $q\geq 1$: $\lim_{t\to 0}(\mu([(h_K^q+tf)^{1/q}])-\mu(K))/t=\frac{1}{q}\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}f(u)dS^\mu_{K,q}(u)$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Removal of constant for $\alpha$-homogeneous $\mu$, $\alpha\neq q$
nodes.statement:
For $q\geq 1$ and even, $\alpha$-homogeneous $\mu$, $\alpha>0$, $\alpha
eq q$, and finite even $
u$ not on a hemisphere, there is symmetric $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $d
u=dS^\mu_{K,q}$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Minkowski's Inequality for $F$-concave Measures
nodes.statement: Fix $q\geq 1$. If $\mu$ is $F$-concave w.r.t. $L^q$ summation with $F$ differentiable on $\mathcal{C}$, then for $K,L\in\mathcal{C}$: $\mu_q(K,L)\geq\mu_q(K,K)+(F(\mu(L))-F(\mu(K)))/F'(\mu(K))$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Minkowski's Inequality - Concavity link
nodes.statement: Equality in $L^q$ Minkowski's inequality (TP456.17) holds iff equality in the $L^q$-$F$-concavity inequality (Equation~\ref{eq:fcon_q}).

nodes.name: Roysdon-Xing concavity-promotion via $L^q$
nodes.statement: If a Radon $\mu$ is $p$-concave w.r.t. Minkowski addition, then for $q\geq 1$ it is $pq$-concave w.r.t. $L^q$ Minkowski addition; for $q>1$, equality forces $A=aB$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ mixed-measure bounds for $p$-concave $\mu$
nodes.statement: For $q>1$ and Radon $p$-concave $\mu$, several $L^q$-mixed-measure inequalities hold; if $\mu$ is also $\alpha$-homogeneous, $\mu_q^\alpha(K,L)\geq(\alpha/q)^\alpha\mu(K)^{\alpha-q}\mu(L)^q$, with equality iff $K=aL$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ uniqueness for $\alpha$-homogeneous, $p$-concave
nodes.statement: Fix $q\geq 1$. If a Radon $\mu$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous, $p$-concave with $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p\in\{q/\alpha,1/\alpha\}$, then $dS^\mu_{K,q}=dS^\mu_{L,q}$ implies $K=L$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Existence and Uniqueness
nodes.statement:
For $q\geq 1$, even Radon $\mu$ that is $p$-concave, $\alpha$-homogeneous with $\alpha
eq q$ and either $\alpha\geq n,p>0$ or $\alpha<n,p\in\{1/\alpha,q/\alpha\}$, and finite even $
u$ not on a hemisphere: there is a unique symmetric $K\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $d
u=dS^\mu_{K,q}$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ uniqueness inequality from $F$-concavity
nodes.statement: Same statement as PrP456.5 but with $dS^\mu_{K,q}=dS^\mu_{L,q}$ in place of $dS^\mu_K=dS^\mu_L$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ uniqueness from monotone-derivative $F$
nodes.statement: Same statement as LP456.3 but with $dS^\mu_{K,q}=dS^\mu_{L,q}$.

nodes.name: $L^q$ Gaussian uniqueness on $\{\gamma_n\geq 1/2\}$
nodes.statement: For $q\geq 1$ and $K,L\in\mathcal{K}^n_0$ with $\gamma_n(K),\gamma_n(L)\geq 1/2$ and $dS^{\gamma_n}_{K,q}=dS^{\gamma_n}_{L,q}$, $K=L$.
